newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all gain, bar illiquid naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all gain, bar illiquid naphtha.

text.p: European oil swaps were firmer across the board, except for naphtha which was unable to capitalise on the screen crude's resurgence because a industry function thinned market liquidity.
CFDs firmed several cents, gasoline made up to $3 and fuel gained $1 or so.

Brent CFDs were firmer by up to 10 cents on close-in contracts, but only by a couple of cents further out. June 30-July 4 was pegged at -26 cents against Brent from -37 cents on Thursday and a CFD traded earlier in the day at -30 cents.
July 7-11 saw a lot of action with trades done at -26 cents, -28 cent, -30 cents, and -31 cents. On Thursday levels were assessed at -37 cents.
July 13-18 was put at -28/29 cents from -34 cents and -30 cents traded. July 21-25 firmed by only one cent or so with levels seen at -29 cents against August from -30 cents.
A July 28-August 1 CFD traded at September Brent -39 cents.
Heavy fuel saw close in swaps levels gain and further out Q4 and Q198 prices slip a touch. Dealers said there was fair activity in the morning, but that business tailed off after NYMEX opened.

July was heard done at $83.50, $83.75 and $84.00, $1-2 firmer from Thursday. The July/August spread weakened to 75 cents from $1.50 and Q4 was valued around $91.50, about 50 cents off. Dealers had talked yesterday that the spreads would probably slip back as storage companies considered getting involved in the action.
August/September was traded at $1.50 and September/October was talked at $2.00 as were October/November.
Fourth quarter high-low talk was of $7.50-$8.00, but nothing was thought concluded.
Low sulphur swaps saw July tick up to 50 cents or so to $93.50-$93.75 with August put at $94.50 and Q4 at $99.25 or so.
Gas oil swaps rallied on rumours of difficulties at the Baltic port of Ventspils with values gaining 50 cents or so. Dealers said 0.2 July heating swaps went at $1.50 and $1.75.
Jet swaps were pretty steady with levels around $19.00 for July and $1.00 contangoed for August and September.

Gasoline swaps were drawn up to $3 higher by crude and NYMEX unleaded futures. The prospect of an open arb to the U.S. was looking more promising and this helped the bullish sentiment. July was put at $183.50 with August backwardated by $1 and September backwardated another $1.
Naphtha swaps were a touch easier, 50 cents or so, amid a lack of key players that kept the market in the doldrums and unable to capitalise on crude's recovery.
